newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia advertisers to spend $2 billion in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia advertisers to spend $2 billion in 1997.

text.p: Growing consumer demand is expected to boost advertising spending in Indonesia to almost five trillion rupiah ($2.06 billion) this year, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Monday.

The paper quoted the Chairman of the Association of Indonesian Advertising Companies (PPPI) Yusca Ismail as saying that 1997 expenditures would increase by around 20 percent from the 4.41 trillion rupiah spent by the industry in 1996.

Ismail said about 2.27 trillion rupiah, or 55 percent, of estimated advertising expenditures would go to television, while 1.34 trillion rupiah, or 27 percent, would be spent on newspaper advertisments.
The balance would be split between magazines (325 billion rupiah), billboards (307 billion rupiah), radio (206 billion) and cinemas (9 billion), he added.
"This is a short term prediction based on fluctuations that always prevail in the industry," Ismail, who is also general manager of the Perwanal advertising agency, was quoted as saying.

He said the industry had initially enjoyed growth rates of up to 40 percent per year since 1989 when the government allowed television stations to air advertisements, but he predicted annual growth rates would decline to around 20 to 25 percent in coming years.
